plan: This is a second-price auction where bidding my true value is the dominant strategy. Since I pay the second-highest bid (not my own bid) if I win, bidding exactly my value of $31 maximizes my expected profit - I win whenever my value exceeds others' bids and pay less than my value, and I don't want to risk winning at a price above my value or losing a profitable opportunity. No history exists to suggest deviation from this optimal strategy.

This is a second-price auction where my bid determines whether I win, and I pay the second-highest bid if I win. The dominant strategy in a second-price auction is to bid exactly my true value, as this maximizes my expected profit regardless of others' bidding strategies. Bidding higher than my value risks winning at a loss, while bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. Since my value is $37, I will bid exactly $37.

This is a second-price auction where the winning bidder pays the second-highest bid. In such auctions, the dominant strategy is to bid exactly my true value, regardless of what others do. Bidding higher risks paying more than the item is worth to me if I win; bidding lower risks losing auctions I could have profitably won. With a value of $11, bidding $11 ensures I maximize expected profit - I'll win whenever the second-highest bid is below $11 and pay exactly that amount, capturing the surplus.
